learning.why: Teacher's chocolate example and now watermelon question made me see I must count all equal parts.

end.summary:
Practised recognising equal parts and naming halves, thirds and quarters.
Compared 1/2, 1/3 and 1/4 of the same whole using group size.
Found 1/2 of 10, 1/3 of 12 and 1/4 of 20 by making equal groups.
Initially described a fraction using parts taken versus parts left; this was corrected later in the lesson.
Teach-back was not completed.
end.parentNote: Nisha practised fractions as equal shares by drawing or imagining equal groups, comparing unit fractions, and finding fractions of collections. They explained that more people sharing the same whole means smaller pieces, and correctly separated the fraction 1/4 from the number of bottles, 6, by the end. At home, use small groups of objects to ask, “What is 1/2, 1/3, or 1/4 of this collection?” and have Nisha make equal groups.
